en.research.head.title: Research Themes
en.research.head.lead: Our research program integrates method development, systems-level analysis, and translational intervention across tumor biology and molecular medicine.
en.research.explore.title: Explore
en.research.explore.subtitle: Functional Nucleic Acid Intelligence
en.research.explore.body: Through the deep integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven computer vision and high-throughput multimodal data analysis, we aim to build a next-generation platform for targeted nucleic acid delivery to cell surface molecules. By overcoming technical bottlenecks and enabling de novo design and high-throughput screening, we will generate high-performance molecular tool libraries, laying the core foundation for constructing high-resolution cellular atlases.
en.research.decode.title: Decode
en.research.decode.subtitle: Frontier Omics Technologies
en.research.decode.body: Focusing on major cancers such as pancreatic cancer and breast cancer, we leverage independently developed functional nucleic acid tools, including nucleic acid adaptors, and integrate them with advanced omics technologies. We develop single-cell (surface) proteomics, interactomics, and spatial multi-omics technologies to construct panoramic, high-resolution molecular maps of tumor initiation and progression, and systematically dissect the key driving mechanisms underlying tumor evolution.
en.research.protect.title: Protect
en.research.protect.subtitle: Precision Diagnosis and Therapeutic Translation
en.research.protect.body: Based on the precise identification of key cell surface molecules and their interactions that drive tumor progression, we develop novel membrane protein-targeted intervention strategies and innovative cell-based therapies. In collaboration with clinical partners, we establish a closed-loop system from multi-omics detection to clinical intervention, providing implementable solutions for personalized medicine and illuminating the path toward improved patient outcomes.

en.research.detail.aptamer.meta.title: New Aptamer Screening for Targeting Protein Interactions | Wu Lab
en.research.detail.aptamer.meta.description: New aptamer screening for targeting protein interactions.
en.research.detail.aptamer.title: New Aptamer Screening for Targeting Protein Interactions
en.research.detail.aptamer.body.html:
Transcription factors (TFs) are widely recognized as key drivers of disease initiation and progression, yet drugging them has long faced two major hurdles: the lack of conventional small-molecule binding pockets and delivery barriers caused by nuclear localization. To address this “undruggable” challenge, we developed an innovative aptamer-based intervention strategy. These nucleic acid molecules, with large molecular size and broad binding surfaces, can effectively block protein–protein interactions (PPIs) and show strong cellular penetration.

Building on this concept, we proposed a structure-guided inhibitory aptamer screening strategy (Blocker-SELEX) to rationally design inhibitory aptamers (iAptamers) targeting TF interaction interfaces. This work, titled “Blocker-SELEX: a structure-guided strategy for developing inhibitory aptamers disrupting undruggable transcription factor interactions,” was published in Nature Communications in 2024, with Tongqing Li (PhD candidate) and Xueying Liu (PhD) as co-first authors.

Using this in-house platform, we targeted aberrant interactions within the SCAF4/SCAF8-RNAP2 transcriptional regulatory complex in triple-negative breast cancer and developed the PTf-SRiApt aptamer. We found that it specifically disrupts SCAF4/SCAF8-RNAP2 interactions in cells, modulates downstream gene expression, significantly suppresses tumor cell proliferation, and further induces neoantigen production by perturbing RNA splicing to activate antitumor immune responses. This systematic study highlights the unique value of iAptamers for intervening in pathogenic TF interactions and provides new directions for nucleic acid drug development. The work, titled “PTf-SRiApt Targeting SCAF4-POLR2A Interaction Suppresses Tumor Growth and Promotes Antitumor Immunity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer,” was published in Advanced Science in 2025, with Liyan Fei, Yichun Pan, and Jie Zhai as co-first authors.
en.research.detail.single.meta.title: Single-Cell Aptamer Sequencing Technology | Wu Lab
en.research.detail.single.title: Single-Cell Aptamer Sequencing Technology
en.research.detail.single.body.html:
With the rapid development of high-throughput sequencing, life science research is moving from qualitative descriptions toward precise quantitative analysis. Yet direct detection of non-nucleic-acid biomolecules such as proteins and glycans remains technically challenging, limiting the construction of multi-dimensional molecular maps. To address this, we developed aptamer sequencing (Apt-seq), enabling high-throughput parallel quantification of proteins, glycosylation modifications, and transcriptomes at the single-cell level for the first time.

We introduced the concept of “Aptomics,” integrating the high-specificity recognition of aptamers with high-throughput sequencing to establish a new multi-omics analysis framework. Using a sialic-acid-specific aptamer, we dynamically captured glycosylation remodeling during T cell differentiation: sialic acid levels rise markedly upon activation of resting T cells and decline at terminal differentiation. This reveals a key role of glycosylation in immune activation regulation.

The Apt-seq platform breaks the quantitative barrier for non-nucleic-acid molecules and enables simultaneous profiling of diverse biomolecules that are directly or indirectly sequenceable. It provides a powerful tool for decoding complex biological systems such as tumor heterogeneity, advancing quantitative life sciences. This work, titled “High-Throughput Multiplexed Quantification of Molecules by Aptamer Sequencing (Apt-seq) in Single Cells,” was published in Journal of the American Chemical Society (JACS) in 2025, with Xiaoqiu Wu as first author.
en.research.detail.tnbc.meta.title: New Therapeutic Targets for TNBC | Wu Lab
en.research.detail.tnbc.meta.description: New therapeutic targets for triple-negative breast cancer.
en.research.detail.tnbc.title: New Therapeutic Targets for TNBC
en.research.detail.tnbc.body.html:
Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2 overexpression, making it largely unresponsive to current targeted therapies and prone to rapid progression. While paclitaxel plays a key role in early-stage or metastatic TNBC, most patients develop resistance after 5–7 months of treatment, leading to disease worsening. To address this challenge, a screen of epigenetic small-molecule inhibitor libraries identified protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs), which regulate RNA splicing and chromatin stability, as new targets for overcoming paclitaxel resistance. The mechanism involves altered RNA splicing, particularly intron retention of Aurora kinase B (AURKB), leading to reduced protein expression and selective induction of mitotic catastrophe in paclitaxel-resistant cells.

Building on our previous discoveries that RNA splicing regulates innate immune mechanisms in TNBC (Nature Chemical Biology 18, 821–830, 2022; Nature Chemical Biology 18, 795–796, 2022), this study further explored the role of RNA splicing in TNBC drug resistance and provides a new therapeutic strategy. The work, titled “A chemical screen identifies PRMT5 as a therapeutic vulnerability for paclitaxel-resistant triple-negative breast cancer,” was published in Cell Chemical Biology in 2024, with Kejing Zhang, Juan Wei, and Sheyu Zhang as co-first authors.

Based on this innovative platform, our lab was invited by Cell to contribute a methods paper detailing experimental protocols and standardized workflows for PRMT5-targeted therapy. The methods paper was published in STAR Protocols in 2025, with Juan Wei and Sheyu Zhang as co-first authors.

zh.research.head.title: 研究方向
zh.research.head.lead: 我们的研究围绕肿瘤生物学与分子医学，整合方法开发、系统解析与临床转化干预。
zh.research.explore.title: 探索
zh.research.explore.subtitle: 功能核酸智能
zh.research.explore.body: 通过深度融合人工智能驱动的计算机视觉与高通量多模态数据分析，我们致力于建立面向细胞表面分子的下一代靶向核酸递送平台。通过突破技术瓶颈并实现从头设计与高通量筛选，我们将获得高性能分子工具库，为构建高分辨率细胞图谱奠定核心基础。
zh.research.decode.title: 解码
zh.research.decode.subtitle: 前沿组学技术
zh.research.decode.body: 围绕胰腺癌、乳腺癌等重大肿瘤，我们依托自主开发的功能核酸工具，并与先进组学技术深度结合，发展单细胞（表面）蛋白组学、互作组学和空间多组学技术，构建肿瘤发生发展的全景式高分辨率分子图谱，系统解析驱动肿瘤演化的关键机制。
zh.research.protect.title: 转化
zh.research.protect.subtitle: 精准诊疗与治疗转化
zh.research.protect.body: 基于对驱动肿瘤进展的关键细胞表面分子及其相互作用的精准识别，我们发展新型膜蛋白靶向干预策略和创新细胞治疗方案，并与临床合作团队共同建立从多组学检测到临床干预的闭环体系，为个体化医疗提供可实施的解决方案。

zh.research.detail.aptamer.meta.title: 靶向蛋白互作的适体筛选新方法 | 吴芩课题组
zh.research.detail.aptamer.meta.description: 靶向蛋白互作的适体筛选新方法。
zh.research.detail.aptamer.title: 靶向蛋白互作的适体筛选新方法
zh.research.detail.aptamer.body.html:
转录因子（Transcription Factors, TFs）在疾病发生发展中的关键作用已获广泛认知，然而其作为药物靶点的开发长期面临两大挑战：一是缺乏传统小分子可靶向的结合口袋，二是核定位特性导致的递送障碍。针对这一“不可成药”难题，我们创新性地开发了基于核酸适配体（aptamer）的干预策略——这类具有较大分子量和广域结合表面的核酸分子，不仅能有效阻断蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPI），还具备优异的细胞穿透能力。

基于此，我们提出“结构引导的阻断型适配体筛选策略”（Blocker-SELEX），通过理性设计靶向 TF 相互作用界面的抑制性核酸适配体（inhibitory aptamer, iAptamer）。该成果以《Blocker-SELEX: a structure-guided strategy for developing inhibitory aptamers disrupting undruggable transcription factor interactions》为题，于 2024 年发表于 Nature Communications，课题组李同庆博士研究生与刘雪莹博士为共同第一作者。

利用上述自主开发的技术平台，我们针对三阴性乳腺癌中 SCAF4/SCAF8-RNAP2 转录调控复合物的异常互作，成功开发出 PTf-SRiApt 适配体。研究发现其可以在细胞内特异性阻断 SCAF4/SCAF8-RNAP2 相互作用，调控下游基因表达，显著抑制肿瘤细胞增殖，并进一步通过干扰 RNA 剪接过程诱导新抗原产生，激活抗肿瘤免疫应答通路。这项系统性研究不仅证实了 iAptamers 在干预致病性 TF 互作中的独特价值，也为核酸药物开发提供了新思路。该成果以《PTf-SRiApt Targeting SCAF4-POLR2A Interaction Suppresses Tumor Growth and Promotes Antitumor Immunity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer》为题，于 2025 年发表于 Advanced Science，课题组费立言同学、潘艺春博士和翟洁博士为论文共同第一作者。
zh.research.detail.single.meta.title: 单细胞核酸适体测序新技术 | 吴芩课题组
zh.research.detail.single.meta.description: 单细胞核酸适体测序新技术。
zh.research.detail.single.title: 单细胞核酸适体测序新技术
zh.research.detail.single.body.html:
随着高通量测序技术的快速发展，生命科学研究正逐步从定性描述转向精准定量分析。然而，蛋白质、糖类等非核酸生物分子的直接检测仍面临技术瓶颈，制约了多维度分子图谱的构建。为此，本研究开发了核酸适体测序（Aptamer sequencing, Apt-seq）技术，首次在单细胞水平实现蛋白质、糖基化修饰及转录组的高通量并行定量。

我们创新性提出“核酸适体组学（Aptomics）”概念，通过整合核酸适体的高特异性识别与高通量测序技术，建立了新型多组学解析体系。应用唾液酸特异性适体，我们动态捕获了 T 细胞分化过程中的糖基化重塑规律：静息 T 细胞激活时唾液酸水平显著上调，而在终末分化阶段回落。该现象揭示了糖基化修饰在免疫活化调控中的关键作用。

Apt-seq 平台成功突破了非核酸分子定量壁垒，可同步解析直接或间接可测序的多元生物分子，为肿瘤异质性等复杂生物系统的精准解密提供了强大工具，有力推进生命科学定量化进程。该成果以《High-Throughput Multiplexed Quantification of Molecules by Aptamer Sequencing (Apt-seq) in Single Cells》为题，于 2025 年发表于 Journal of the American Chemical Society（JACS），课题组武晓秋博士为论文第一作者。
zh.research.detail.tnbc.meta.title: 三阴性乳腺癌治疗新靶点发现 | 吴芩课题组
zh.research.detail.tnbc.meta.description: 三阴性乳腺癌治疗新靶点发现。
zh.research.detail.tnbc.title: 三阴性乳腺癌治疗新靶点发现
zh.research.detail.tnbc.body.html:
三阴性乳腺癌因其缺乏雌激素受体、孕激素受体和 HER2 过表达，通常对现有靶向治疗无效，且病情进展迅速。虽然紫杉醇在治疗早期或转移性 TNBC 患者中起到了关键作用，但大部分患者在接受治疗 5–7 个月后会出现耐药性，导致疾病恶化。为应对这一挑战，我们通过表观遗传小分子抑制剂库筛选，成功鉴定出调控 RNA 剪接和染色质稳定性的蛋白精氨酸甲基转移酶（PRMTs），将其确立为克服紫杉醇耐药性的新靶点。其主要机制是改变 RNA 剪接，尤其导致 Aurora 激酶 B（AURKB）内含子保留，进而降低蛋白表达，并在耐紫杉醇细胞中选择性诱导有丝分裂灾难。

基于课题组此前关于 RNA 剪接调控三阴性乳腺癌内源免疫机制的研究发现（Nature Chemical Biology 18, 821–830, 2022；Nature Chemical Biology 18, 795–796, 2022），本研究进一步揭示了 RNA 剪接参与 TNBC 耐药性的全新机制，为 TNBC 治疗提供了新的策略。该成果以《A chemical screen identifies PRMT5 as a therapeutic vulnerability for paclitaxel-resistant triple-negative breast cancer》为题，于 2024 年发表于 Cell Chemical Biology，课题组张克兢博士、魏娟和张舍予同学为论文共同第一作者。

基于该创新技术体系，课题组受 Cell 期刊特邀撰写技术方法论文，系统阐述 PRMT5 靶向治疗策略的实验方案与标准化流程。相关方法学成果于 2025 年发表于 STAR Protocols，课题组魏娟和张舍予同学为论文共同第一作者。
